name: The keyboard map
explanation: The keyboard repeats the same seven white-key names, C through B. The black keys come in groups of two and three — C always sits just left of a group of two.
examples: C is left of the two black keys
F is left of the three black keys

questions.promptText: Which key sits just LEFT of every group of TWO black keys?
questions.explanation: C always sits just left of the two black keys — that's the fastest way to find it anywhere.

questions.promptText: Which key sits just LEFT of every group of THREE black keys?
questions.explanation: F sits just left of the three black keys.

questions.promptText: How many different white-key NAMES are there before the pattern repeats?
questions.explanation: Seven names — C D E F G A B — then the pattern starts over an octave higher.

questions.promptText: You're on C and step UP one white key. Where are you?
questions.explanation: Stepping up from C lands on D — names go up the alphabet as you go right.

questions.promptText: Two keys with the same name, eight steps apart, are called…
questions.explanation: Same name, higher or lower — that distance is an octave.

questions.promptText: Higher-sounding notes live in which direction on the keyboard?
questions.explanation: Right = higher, left = lower. Your ear and the map agree.

name: Beat, bar, and downbeat
explanation: The beat is the steady pulse you'd tap your foot to. Beats group into bars, and the first beat of each bar — the downbeat — carries a little extra weight.

questions.promptText: The steady pulse you tap your foot to is called the…
questions.explanation: That's the beat — everything else in the music lines up against it.

questions.promptText: The FIRST beat of every bar is called the…
questions.explanation: Beat 1 is the downbeat — it's where the bar 'lands'.

questions.promptText: You count '1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4…'. What happens at every '1'?
questions.explanation: Each count of 1 is the start of a new bar — the downbeat.

questions.promptText: If you play a wrong note, the best move for the groove is to…
choices: Keep going and land the next beat
questions.explanation: Musicians keep the pulse. Recover on the next beat — nobody hears the note you didn't replay.

questions.promptText: A metronome is for practicing your…
questions.explanation: The click is an honest timing mirror — that's why the app scores timing, not just notes.

name: Common time — 4/4
explanation: A time signature describes the bar: the TOP number says how many beats each bar has; the BOTTOM number says which note value counts as one beat. 4/4 — 'common time' — means four quarter-note beats per bar.

questions.promptText: In a time signature, the TOP number tells you…
questions.explanation: Top number = beats per bar. In 4/4 you count to four, then a new bar starts.

questions.promptText: In 4/4, the BOTTOM 4 means one beat lasts a…
questions.explanation: The bottom number names the note value of the beat — 4 means quarter note.

questions.promptText: A 4/4 bar so far holds three quarter notes. What single note completes it?
questions.explanation: Three beats are used, one is left — one more quarter note fills the bar.

questions.promptText: You hear: ONE-two-three-four, ONE-two-three-four. The meter is…
questions.explanation: An accent every four beats is the sound of 4/4 — common time.

questions.promptText: How many quarter notes fit in TWO bars of 4/4?
questions.explanation: Four per bar × two bars = eight.

name: Tier 1 check: keys, beats, and bars
explanation: Everything Tier 1 taught, in one short check: the keyboard map, the beat, and 4/4 time.

questions.promptText: Which key sits just left of the two black keys?
questions.explanation: C — left of every pair of black keys.

questions.promptText: In 4/4 time, how many beats are in each bar?
questions.explanation: Four quarter-note beats per bar.

questions.promptText: The first beat of a bar is the…
questions.explanation: The downbeat — count '1'.

questions.promptText: Notes get HIGHER as you move which way?
questions.explanation: Rightward = higher pitch, always.

questions.promptText: Stepping up one white key from E lands on…
questions.explanation: E steps up to F — they're direct neighbors with no black key between.

questions.promptText: A 4/4 bar already has two quarter notes and one half note. It is…
questions.explanation: 2 + 2 = 4 beats — the bar is complete.

questions.promptText: If you miss a note mid-song, you should…
choices: Keep the pulse and catch the next beat
Play it twice to make up
questions.explanation: Keeping the pulse is the skill. Recovery beats perfection.

questions.promptText: Two notes sound in a row and the second is lower. It moved…
questions.explanation: Lower sound = downward movement = leftward on the keys.
